# Installation Guide

**Project:** FleetPulse · **Student:** Hafsa Aqeel (53317)
**Generated by AI prompt:** P-20, then verified by performing a clean install.

---

## 1. Prerequisites

| Requirement | Version | Check |
|---|---|---|
| Python | 3.11 or newer (tested on 3.14) | `python3 --version` |
| Node.js | 18 or newer (tested on 25) | `node --version` |
| npm | 9 or newer | `npm --version` |

No database server, message broker, Docker daemon or internet connection is required.
FleetPulse uses SQLite (a single file) and the dashboard draws its own map, so the whole
project runs offline.

---

## 2. Install

### macOS / Linux

```bash
cd hafsa-gen-ai-final

# Backend
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r backend/requirements.txt

# Frontend
cd frontend && npm install && cd ..
```

### Windows (PowerShell)

> A fuller Windows walkthrough — Docker Desktop, the CRLF trap, PowerShell's `curl` alias and
> a troubleshooting table — is in [`WINDOWS.md`](../WINDOWS.md).

```powershell
cd hafsa-gen-ai-final

python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r backend\requirements.txt

cd frontend; npm install; cd ..
```

If PowerShell refuses to run the activate script:
`Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass`

---

## 3. Create the demo data

```bash
cd backend
python -m app.seed --reset
```

Expected output:

```
seeded 3 routes, 12 vehicles, 8 deliveries
```

This creates `backend/fleetpulse.db`: two bus routes with timetabled stops, one truck
route, eight buses and four refrigerated trucks. No telemetry is seeded — the simulator
produces it live, so the demo starts from an explainable clean state.

---

## 4. Run

Three terminals, all from the repository root with the virtualenv activated where noted.

**Terminal 1 — API** (virtualenv active)

```bash
cd backend
uvicorn app.main:app --reload
```

→ API on <http://127.0.0.1:8000>, interactive docs on <http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs>

**Terminal 2 — dashboard**

```bash
cd frontend
npm run dev
```

→ dashboard on <http://localhost:5173> (Vite proxies `/api` and `/ws` to port 8000, so
there is nothing to configure)

**Terminal 3 — simulator** (virtualenv active)

```bash
cd backend
python -m app.simulate
```

→ twelve vehicles begin reporting every 5 seconds; the dashboard fills in within a tick.

Stop everything with `Ctrl+C` in each terminal.

---

## 5. Simulator options

```bash
python -m app.simulate --help
```

| Flag | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--api URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:8000` | Where to post telemetry |
| `--seed N` | `42` | Deterministic run — the same seed reproduces the same readings |
| `--interval S` | `5.0` | Seconds between ticks |
| `--ticks N` | `0` | `0` runs until interrupted |
| `--scenario CODE=NAME` | — | Arm a fault; repeatable |
| `--gtfs URL` | — | Ingest a real GTFS-Realtime feed instead of simulating |
| `--gtfs-prefix P` | `""` | Prefix mapped onto GTFS vehicle ids |

Scenarios: `overheat`, `fuel_drain`, `deviation`, `dropout`, `cargo_spike`, `none`.

```bash
python -m app.simulate \
  --scenario BUS-03=overheat \
  --scenario TRK-01=cargo_spike \
  --scenario BUS-05=deviation \
  --scenario BUS-07=dropout \
  --scenario BUS-02=fuel_drain
```

Each armed fault ramps rather than jumping, so an examiner watches the value climb through
its threshold. Approximate time to the first alert at the default 5-second tick:

| Scenario | Alert | Appears after |
|---|---|---|
| `overheat` | `ENGINE_OVERHEAT` warning → critical | ~50 s → ~90 s |
| `deviation` | `ROUTE_DEVIATION` | ~60 s |
| `cargo_spike` | `CARGO_TEMP_EXCURSION` | ~60 s |
| `fuel_drain` | `LOW_FUEL` | ~90 s |
| `dropout` | `VEHICLE_OFFLINE` | ~2.5 min (heartbeat timeout 120 s + sweep interval) |

## 6. Run the tests

The AI-generated suite is the mandatory constraint for this project (Python → AI must
auto-generate tests).

```bash
cd backend
pytest                      # runs everything, prints coverage
pytest tests/test_rules_overspeed.py -v     # one rule
pytest -k "deduplicat"                      # by name
open htmlcov/index.html                     # browsable coverage report
```

Expected: **290 passed**, total coverage ≈ 87%, rule-engine coverage ≈ 99%.

## 7. Production build of the dashboard

```bash
cd frontend
npm run build      # emits dist/
npm run preview    # serves the built bundle
```

Serving `dist/` from any static host works, provided `/api` and `/ws` are reverse-proxied
to the FastAPI process.

---

## 8. Configuration

Every setting has a working default. Override with environment variables before starting
the API:

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `FLEETPULSE_DATABASE_URL` | `sqlite:///./fleetpulse.db` | Any SQLAlchemy URL; PostgreSQL works unchanged |
| `FLEETPULSE_RETENTION_DAYS` | `7` | Default window for the prune endpoint |
| `FLEETPULSE_OFFLINE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_S` | `20` | How often the offline sweeper runs |
| `FLEETPULSE_MAX_BATCH_SIZE` | `500` | Batch ingestion cap |
| `FLEETPULSE_DISABLE_SWEEPER` | unset | Set to `1` to disable the background sweeper |
| `FLEETPULSE_LOG_LEVEL` | `INFO` | Standard logging level |
| `FLEETPULSE_ENGINE_WARN_C` etc. | see `app/config.py` | Starting values for every rule threshold |

Thresholds can also be changed at runtime from the dashboard's Settings page, with no
restart (FR-22).

Using PostgreSQL instead of SQLite:

```bash
pip install "psycopg[binary]"
export FLEETPULSE_DATABASE_URL="postgresql+psycopg://user:pass@localhost/fleetpulse"
python -m app.seed --reset
```

---

## 9. Optional — real GTFS-Realtime data

The GTFS path is optional on purpose: an unavailable protobuf wheel must never block
installation (FR-37).

```bash
pip install gtfs-realtime-bindings
python -m app.simulate --gtfs https://your-agency.example/gtfs-rt/vehicle-positions \
                       --gtfs-prefix KHI-
```

Vehicles in the feed must first be registered in FleetPulse with matching codes
(`<prefix><gtfs vehicle id>`); unregistered ids are reported in the batch response's
`rejected` count rather than being silently created.

Without the package installed, the reader raises a clear `GtfsUnavailable` message and the
rest of the system carries on.

---

## 10. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `no vehicles found — run python -m app.seed first` | Empty database | `python -m app.seed --reset` |
| Dashboard shows "polling (ws down)" | API not running, or the WebSocket was blocked | Start the API; the SPA reconnects automatically and keeps working via polling meanwhile |
| Dashboard is empty but the API responds | Simulator not running | Start terminal 3 |
| `Address already in use` | Port 8000 or 5173 taken | `uvicorn app.main:app --port 8001` and update `frontend/vite.config.js` |
| Simulator prints `post failed` | API not up yet | Wait for uvicorn to report "Application startup complete", then retry |
| Every bus shows `SCHEDULE_DELAY` immediately | Stale database seeded by an older build | `python -m app.seed --reset` |
| `ModuleNotFoundError: app` | Running from the wrong directory | All `python -m app.*` commands run from `backend/` |
